cases.title: Profitable OEM instrument maker, temporary dip, leverage 2.1x, family stake 31%
reasons: Segment fits: Northline makes OEM analyzer systems, which is in-vitro diagnostics (instruments and OEM analyzers), so it is not a Watch on segment grounds.
Business model fits: consumables and service are 62% of sales, above the 50% threshold for recurring revenue.
Kill criteria are not met on the facts given: net debt is 2.1x EBITDA, below the 4x limit; no major regulatory issue is reported.

The price drop looks temporary: the 38% fall over 12 months follows a platform launch that slipped two quarters. The first platform shipments are done and H1 order intake is recovering. This is consistent with a product transition, not a structural loss of market. The evidence is one H1 release, so it is supportive but not conclusive.
Ownership flag: the founding family (Northline Beteiligungs) holds 31%, above the 25% threshold. The rule is flag-only, so this does not reject the company.

Key fact unknown: the family has made no public statement about its stake. Because the rule rejects only if a controlling holder has ruled out a sale, silence does not trigger a reject. But the family's willingness to sell decides whether a take-private is feasible at all. Under the rule that an unknown fact is never a pass, this keeps the verdict at Watch rather than Fit.
What would move it to Fit: confirmation that the family is open to a sale, or at least that it has not ruled one out. A Reject would follow only if the family publicly ruled out a sale.

cases.title: Profitable, cheap, but the market is going away
reasons: Segment criterion met: rapid antigen tests for respiratory viruses are in-vitro diagnostics, one of the segments the thesis likes (instruments, assays, OEM analyzers, lab automation).

The price drop is most likely structural, which the thesis places under Watch, not Fit. Revenue has fallen for three consecutive years, the latest release shows a further 30% decline, and the cause is pandemic-era testing volume disappearing. That is a loss of demand for the product category, not a temporary product transition, customer destocking or one-off charge. Management also has no new product with meaningful sales, so there is no visible recovery catalyst.

Business model criterion is not demonstrated. The facts do not show that recurring revenue (consumables under supply contracts, service) is at least half of sales. Rapid tests are typically sold as one-off orders, and the profile says nothing about supply contracts. This is unknown, not a pass. It only generates a warning and cannot cause a reject, but it is a missing key fact.

Kill criteria are not met. Net debt is 0.4x EBITDA, well below the 4x threshold, using the figure from the data. No controlling shareholder is named, and the facts state there is no major regulatory issue. Nothing in the profile triggers a reject.

Ownership rule: no holder is above 25%. Top holder Vanguard holds 9% and insiders hold 4%. Nothing to flag under the 25% rule, and no owner has ruled out a sale. The absence of a large holder means the take-private would need a negotiated deal with dispersed shareholders, which is a deal-execution question, not a kill criterion.

Profitability is positive. The 24% LTM EBITDA margin is solid and has been sustained by cost cuts. That supports the cash-flow side of the thesis, but the thesis asks for a temporary decline. Margins held up through cost reduction on a shrinking top line, so they do not offset the structural revenue problem.

Price action is consistent with the fundamentals: -62% over 12 months and -18% over 3 months. The market appears to be pricing in permanent demand loss, which is the opposite of the thesis premise that the decline is temporary.

Conclusion: no kill criterion is met, so this is not a Reject. The thesis criteria are not met, because the revenue decline looks structural and the recurring-revenue share is unknown. It is therefore not a Fit. It should be re-evaluated if management shows a replacement product with meaningful sales, if the company discloses a recurring supply or service share of at least 50%, or if the revenue decline is shown to be a temporary destocking effect.

cases.title: Real data: QuidelOrtho (QDEL), net debt 6.1x EBITDA
reasons: Kill criterion met: net debt / EBITDA is 6.09x (debt 3,076m USD, cash 123m USD, TTM EBITDA 485m USD), above the 4x limit. The thesis says this figure comes from the data and is not computed by the judge. Under the verdict rules, any kill criterion means Reject, whatever the other criteria say.

Sensitivity check, not used for the verdict: the profile's ebitda_margin_ltm (0.181) applied to revenue of 2,386.7m EUR implies EBITDA of about 432m, which would put leverage near 6.8x. The two sources disagree on EBITDA, but both are above 4x, so the verdict does not change.
Segment fits: QuidelOrtho is in immunoassay and point-of-care, which is in-vitro diagnostics. This criterion is met.

Profitability is mixed: TTM EBITDA margin is 18.1%, but fiscal EBITDA was -1,490m USD in 2024 and -483m USD in 2025, after 607m USD in 2023. The dataset does not say what caused these losses, so the 'profitable' test is not clearly met.

Why the price is low is unknown: the share price fell 54.1% over 12 months and 22.1% over 3 months, but the dataset gives no cause. The headlines (2026-10-16 'Shares Plummet', 2026-10-12 'Buy, Sell, or Hold Post Q2 Earnings?') do not explain it. The drop could be temporary (product transition, destocking, one-off charges) or structural. Under the rules this is Watch on its own, and an unknown fact is never a pass.
Recurring revenue share (consumables, service, supply contracts) is not in the dataset. This is a warning only, not a reject, but the criterion is unverified.

Ownership: no holder is above 25%. The largest reported holders are BlackRock (16.3%), FMR (10.7%) and Newtyn Management (9.7%). Insiders hold 0.9%. Yahoo lists at most five institutions, so a family or strategic holder could be missing. Nothing in the dataset says whether any holder has ruled out a sale. Flag only, no reject from this criterion.
Regulatory: the dataset has no information on regulatory matters, so there is no evidence of a major unresolved regulatory issue. This is unknown, not a pass.

Conclusion: the company is rejected on leverage alone. The other open points (price-drop cause, recurring revenue share, regulatory status, possible missing holders) would only be Watch items. The company should not be reconsidered unless leverage falls to 4x or below on verified figures.
